chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The most beloved of deeds to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is bringing joy to a believer: satiating his hunger, relieving his distress, or paying off his debt.
ai.seo_question: What are the most beloved deeds to Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing that alleviating a believer's worldly hardships is a direct path to divine pleasure. This hadith underscores the Shia concept of 'Ihya al-Mawat' (reviving the dead) through social welfare, linking material relief to spiritual merit. It serves as a practical guide for communal solidarity, elevating simple acts of charity to the status of highly beloved deeds in the sight of Allah.
